answer: Accept 'porous solid made from sodium silicate' (silica gel is a form of silicon dioxide, not a salt), so Lesson 6 should not call it a salt. Do not add the NCPB claim that anhydrous CaCl2 tests maize moisture, because maize moisture is measured with a moisture meter or oven drying and the NCPB practice cannot be verified here. Keep the Bata sentence, correct the silica gel wording, and add only a general, true statement that anhydrous calcium chloride is used as a drying agent that takes up water, which the Lesson 6 watch-glass mass gain shows.

edits.old: (silica gel is not deliquescent; it holds water on its surface, but it is used for the same drying purpose)
edits.new: (silica gel is a porous solid made from sodium silicate; it is a form of silicon dioxide, not a salt. It is not deliquescent; it holds water on its surface, but it is used for the same drying purpose)

edits.old: pharmaceutical companies in Nairobi's Industrial Area use silica gel in their packing boxes;
edits.new: pharmaceutical companies in Nairobi's Industrial Area use silica gel in their packing boxes; anhydrous calcium chloride is also used as a drying agent to keep stored goods dry because it takes up water, as our mass-gain data showed (teacher note: it is not a method for measuring maize moisture, which uses a moisture meter or oven drying);

alternative: Drop the NCPB example altogether and keep only the Bata and pharmaceutical silica gel examples.
